note: Both sets cover the same lighting-levels graphic and the Title 24 text, and both repeat nearly every graphic fact twice (with and without the activity condition) and state each bulb fact under two attribute names. Set B binds the bulb counts/wattages to a sensible property (lighting load) and keeps the activity conditions, whereas Set A binds four of them to 'power source', which is the wrong property for a bulb wattage, and one of its quotes misreads the label as 'CONRAST'. Set B's only real defects are one garbled value ('40 W W' with 'at half power' pushed into conditions) and one misread quote ('CONSTRAT'); both sets miss the 40W incandescent / 9W CFL / 7W LED efficacy comparison and the dimmer-switch statements.
remarks: The graphic's column header is printed as 'LARGE SIZE OR HIGH CONSTRACT' (a typo in the source document); Set A's bracketed 'CONSTRAC[T]' is the faithful rendering, while 'CONRAST' (Set A) and 'CONSTRAT' (Set B) are extraction misreads. Both sets omit the text-layer efficacy example (one 40W incandescent = 9W compact fluorescent = 7W LED in light output, LED has higher efficacy), the statement that dimmer switches vary light output and energy consumption, and that low efficacy luminaires may be paired with vacancy sensors and dimmers. Both sets also duplicate essentially every graphic fact under both a conditioned and an unconditioned claim, and restate each bulb fact under two attribute names ('lighting source' plus 'power source'/'lighting load'), inflating the claim counts without adding information.
